method: Full-body key-pose guide, then single opposite-contact diagnostic

records.prompt: Production pixel-game animation atlas, EXACTLY FOUR COLUMNS and ONE ROW on true transparency. Reference 1 is the exact Ticket clerk identity and art style: tousled chestnut hair, small round dark glasses, blue long sleeve sweater with white wave emblem, cream knee-length shorts, BARE skin lower knees, brown low ankle boots, brown diagonal shoulder satchel, one hand grips its strap. Reference 2 is a FOUR POSE FULL BODY walking blueprint, geometry only. Render the Ticket clerk in strict RIGHT-FACING PROFILE, eyes and nose face screen right in every cel. Redraw the WHOLE CHARACTER separately for each of the four guide poses, using its connected hip/knee/ankle geometry and ownership of the near and far leg EXACTLY. In the guide orange is the SAME NEAR LEG in all four cells, blue the SAME FAR LEG. Those colors are annotation only: actual legs are bare skin, boots brown, the far leg shaded slightly darker for depth. Cell 1 near leg forward with forward boot on ground and far leg behind on its toe; Cell 2 NEAR leg supports weight under hip on ground, FAR leg bent and swinging forward off ground; Cell 3 FAR leg forward on ground and NEAR leg behind on toe, an unmistakable opposite contact from Cell 1; Cell 4 FAR leg supports weight under hip on ground, NEAR leg bent swinging forward above ground. Near thigh must visibly connect to near knee, far thigh to far knee, no duplicate lower limb, disconnected ankle, reversed knee or three feet. Hold the satchel strap naturally with the near hand throughout; other arm moves very slightly opposite the legs. Preserve the SAME face, glasses, tousled hair, sweater sleeves, emblem, cream shorts length, bare shin, boots and satchel in all cels. Gentle service-worker walk, no running or giant marching strides; follow the guide proportions only for the leg action, retain reference1 compact head/body proportions. Identical figure scale and grounded-foot baseline in all four equal cells. Distinct alternating support feet, not 4 repeated near-leg-forward poses. Crisp pixel contours, stepped clusters, modest coherent shading matching reference1. 12% transparent outer margins, wide fully transparent gutters between figures; all hair, hands, bag and complete boot soles inside each cell. No guide skeleton, orange/blue leg colors, text, labels, background, floor, grid, cast shadows, extra props, socks or long trousers. Output is only four finished full-body character sprites, not a mechanical rig.
records.reason: Four-cell output repeats A/pass A twice; no alternating support ownership, and soft background alpha.

records.prompt: Create ONE complete full-body sprite of Ticket, facing RIGHT, in the opposite walking contact pose, Contact B. Reference1 locks character identity and style: same tousled chestnut hair, round glasses, blue long sleeved wave-emblem sweater, cream shorts, shoulder bag, compact proportions. Reference2 is a pose blueprint: use its THIRD figure only. This is a diagnostic animation drawing. Temporarily color the ENTIRE CAMERA-NEAR leg and its complete boot ORANGE; temporarily color the ENTIRE CAMERA-FAR leg and its complete boot BLUE. These colors identify anatomical legs, not screen positions. Each leg's color must connect continuously from its cream shorts opening through knee, ankle, and boot. The ORANGE CAMERA-NEAR leg trails BACK toward SCREEN LEFT: its thigh slopes back-left, knee behind the pelvis, heel lifted, boot toe touches the ground BEHIND the body. The BLUE CAMERA-FAR leg reaches FORWARD toward SCREEN RIGHT: knee ahead of the pelvis, heel touching the ground AHEAD of the body. At the hip/thigh overlap, the ORANGE near limb remains IN FRONT of and overlaps the BLUE far limb; orange is not the hidden leg. The visible near shorts opening must be on top at the orange thigh origin, its orange thigh extends to LEFT. This is the opposite of a foreground leg reaching screen-right. Face and torso point screen-right. Draw the complete character directly in this pose, one hand holds bag strap, other hand relaxed. One character only, one pose only, all hair and feet comfortably within canvas, 15% margin. True transparent background, no colored glow, floor, text, labels or guide skeleton. Natural undistorted anatomy. The temporary two leg colors are deliberate diagnostic marks. Everything above the shorts and the bag retains the original finished character colors and rendering.
records.reason: Single diagnostic exposes leg colors but loses strict profile, compact source proportions and pixel rendering; near/far thigh overlap still does not prove opposite contact. No de-color pass or runtime adoption.
